seo_description: Solo audio designer on a 4-player racing game. Procedural MetaSounds engine, priority-based mix for 4 players, and full audio pipeline in 12 weeks.
hero.title: Not Today, Darling!
hero.subtitle: Solo Audio Designer / 4-player side-scrolling racer / 12 weeks
concept.hook: Solo audio designer. 4 players racing at once. 12 weeks to ship everything from scratch.
concept.p1: Not Today, Darling! is a chaotic 4-player side-scrolling racer where grannies race, smash, and scream their way to victory. Power-ups, collisions, and character voices all fire at once — the mix had to stay clear under pressure.
concept.p2: I was the only audio person on the 8-person team. I designed and implemented everything: procedural go-kart engine via MetaSounds, surface-reactive driving sounds, a priority-based Sound Class mix for 4 simultaneous players, and recorded character voices with the team.
systems.engine.title: Procedural Go-Kart Engine
systems.engine.desc: Built in MetaSounds — RPM, throttle, and load drive the engine sound in real-time. No baked loops. The engine responds to player input frame by frame, so it feels connected to the kart.
systems.mix.title: Priority-Based Mix
systems.mix.desc: 4 players means 4 engines, 4 sets of power-ups, collisions, and voices all at once. Sound Classes with priority levels keep the local player's audio on top. Attenuation presets push distant karts into the background.
systems.voices.title: Character Voices
systems.voices.desc: Recorded granny voice lines with the team — reactions to collisions, power-ups, and overtakes. Implemented as randomized Sound Cues with cooldown timers to prevent spam.
challenge1.title: Mix Clarity with 4 Players
challenge1.hard: 4 karts, 4 engines, power-ups, collisions, and voices all playing at once. Without management, everything collapsed into noise — players couldn't tell what was happening to their kart.
challenge1.did: Built a Sound Class hierarchy with priority levels. The local player's kart always sits on top of the mix. Distant karts get attenuated and ducked. Power-up and collision sounds use concurrency limits so only the most relevant ones play.
challenge2.title: Procedural Engine That Feels Right
challenge2.hard: MetaSounds procedural synthesis can sound sterile and disconnected from gameplay. The engine had to respond instantly to throttle changes and feel like it's actually powering the kart.
challenge2.did: Mapped RPM, throttle position, and load directly to MetaSounds parameters. Added pitch smoothing to prevent jarring jumps on sudden input changes. The result tracks player input frame by frame.
